CHIEF COMPLAINT: Mild wheezing and shortness of breath with exertion for 1 week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 22-year-old with new-onset exertional wheezing, no chest pain, no prior history of asthma. Recent cold 2 weeks ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Positive for wheezing and mild dyspnea on exertion. Negative for chest pain, fever, hemoptysis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: No chronic conditions.

VITALS: BP 114/70, HR 80, Temp 98.0F, RR 16, SpO2 97% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Mild expiratory wheeze bilaterally, no accessory muscle use, no cyanosis.

ASSESSMENT: Likely post-viral reactive airway episode versus new-onset mild asthma.
